question.text: A system of three polarizers <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> is set up such that the pass axis of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math> is crossed with respect to that of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></math> . The pass axis of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is inclined at <math><msup><mrow><mn>60</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup></math> to the pass axis of <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></math> When a beam of unpolarized light of intensity <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msub></math> is incident on <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo></math> the intensity of light transmitted by the three polarizers is <math><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> . The ratio <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfenced></math> equals (nearly):

solution.text:
The intensity of light coming out of 1st Polaroid will be I1=I02
From Malus law I=I0cos2⁡θ
From Polaroid 2:   I=I02cos2⁡30°=I02322=3I08
From Polaroid 3: I=3I08cos2⁡60°=3I08122=3I032
